doc.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Jazz appreciation in Europe and expatriate musicians
summary: Europeans appreciate the music, and black musicians like Sidney Bechet were treated better abroad.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: It’s different overseas, it really is. There’s so many more people who really appreciate the music and know about it over there, and that’s not changed since the twenties. The first books on jazz were from Europe.
Right. We had a lot of our jazz musicians booking over there.

Sure. And then they stayed there forever. I mean the black musicians who went there were treated like human beings and didn’t have to look over their shoulder every time, and they had long and productive lives. Sidney Bechet is a God in France still. And I think that’s too bad that in his own country he couldn’t be treated that way.
Well I’m hoping you don’t have to move over there.
Mississippi is about as far as I want to go.
Okay. You can go for a visit.
